name: Jellyfin Security
description: Comprehensive Jellyfin security: TOTP & email 2FA, passkeys, OIDC/SSO sign-in (Google, Microsoft, Apple, Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak, PocketID, Cloudflare Access, ...), brute-force IP banning, impossible-travel detection, per-user IP allowlist, device pairing, trusted browsers, and audit log.
overview: Comprehensive Jellyfin security: 2FA, passkeys, OIDC/SSO, brute-force protection, impossible-travel detection, IP allowlist, and audit logging.

versions.changelog: v2.5.9 - OIDC mobile sign-in + security hardening. Highlight: 'Sign in with Google' (and other OIDC/SSO providers) now works inside the Jellyfin mobile apps - the in-app browser was previously rejected by Google (403 disallowed_useragent) and dead-ended on the server screen; sign-in now opens in the device browser and returns you straight into the app, with per-provider 2FA-bypass preserved (issue #64). This release also includes a broad internal security-hardening pass across the authentication, OIDC/SSO, step-up, device-bypass and rate-limiting paths - no configuration changes or action needed on upgrade. Additionally: the injected login script is now served in a CDN/proxy-cache-safe way so an edge cache can no longer pin a stale copy after an upgrade; GeoIP database path handling is unified across lookups; and assorted reliability and resource-bounding improvements to in-memory sign-in state. In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x, no schema or data migration. 254/254 tests pass on .NET 9 / Jellyfin 10.11.x. Sigstore-signed + SLSA build-provenance attested.

v2.5.8 - Admin step-up UX + smoke-test followups. FIXES: issue #57 (lorenatkin) admin Save Settings now triggers the existing step-up modal instead of silently rejecting when StepUpLevel is set - the main config POST was going through Jellyfin's built-in ApiClient.updatePluginConfiguration which doesn't recognise the 403 + stepUpRequired body, now flows through the same step-up-aware fetch wrapper every other gated admin endpoint uses, so the modal opens, accepts TOTP/recovery/passkey, verifies, and replays the original save transparently. StepUpLevel dropdown enum-name mismatch: Jellyfin's JsonStringEnumConverter serialises the enum by name (Off/Destructive/AllConfigChanges/Everything) but option values were 0/1/2/3 - dropdown went blank after save+refresh and parseInt('') silently posted 0, resetting the level to Off on every Save (which is also why subsequent settings toggles weren't gated). Option values now use enum names directly. Issue #55 followup (Dasnap): Users tab enumerates from Jellyfin's user table instead of plugin-side data files, so users who haven't yet interacted with the plugin show with all-zero counts instead of being invisible. Single-user read failures no longer 500 the whole listing. Issue #56 (cwildfoerster, derpacco): admin Hardening section gets a help block under Trusted Proxy CIDRs explaining the broad-RFC1918-range trap with concrete fix examples. SEC-H3 refusal log promoted from Debug to Information on first hit per peer IP (subsequent hits stay Debug to avoid spam) with the matched CIDR in the payload for self-diagnosis. Pending-pair Approve/Deny/QR buttons no longer fail silently - each click surfaces server errors via alert + console.error. Textarea clipping (LAN CIDRs, Trusted Proxy CIDRs, Admin emails, Exempt CIDRs, Restore JSON paste box) - .tfa-input now uses box-sizing:border-box so width:100% includes padding instead of bleeding outside parent panels. CODE-QUALITY: two CodeQL cs/cleartext-storage-of-sensitive-information false-positives dismissed (CIDRs are admin config, not credentials). UPGRADE: in-place, no schema breakage. If StepUpLevel was set non-Off on v2.5.7 the dropdown bug may have silently reset it - after upgrading + hard-refresh, re-pick the value and Save once. 254/254 tests pass on .NET 9 / Jellyfin 10.11.10. Sigstore-signed + SLSA build-provenance attested.

v2.5.7 - bug-fix and OIDC-experience release. Fixes issue #52 (sessions getting permanently 403'd by RequestBlockerMiddleware after docker compose down/up - verified-token state now persists as SHA-256 hashes in a sidecar so the in-memory set rehydrates on restart instead of locking everyone out), issue #54 (OIDC discovery rejected LAN-only / VPN-only IdPs - new per-provider AllowPrivateNetworks toggle, Advanced/default off, bypasses the v2.5.5 SSRF guard for THAT provider only), issue #55 (Users tab 500'd with Guid.Empty ArgumentException when a junk lockout entry existed - defensive skip in GetUsers plus write-refuse at the store boundary), and issue #50 followup (PR #53 by duongynhi000005-oss - login.html maxlength was still 6 so 8-digit email codes were truncated). Pending-pair Approve / Deny / QR buttons now show a spinner during the request and surface server errors via alert + console instead of silently dying. New: issue #48 feature (Gaarindor) - two independent admin toggles to hide the 'Sign in with 2FA' and 'Sign in with passkey' buttons inject.js adds to Jellyfin's main login page, so OIDC-only deployments look like OIDC-only deployments. New: OIDC step-up factor for users - users with only an IdP linked can satisfy SelfServiceStepUpMode=Forced by re-authenticating to that IdP in a popup, with subject-match against the stored SsoLink to prevent signing into a different account from granting step-up. In-place upgrade, no schema changes. 254/254 tests pass on .NET 9 / Jellyfin 10.11.10. Release artifacts cosign-signed and SLSA-provenance attested.

v2.5.6 - Security and bug-fix release. Critical: closes a stolen-password account-takeover path where a known or guessed client-supplied DeviceId let an attacker skip 2FA via the registered-device / paired-device fallback (the signed trusted-device cookie path was always safe and is unchanged). New BareDeviceIdBypassEnabled config gates the legacy behaviour, default off. Also fixes issue #28 (OIDC redirect_uri built as http behind TLS-terminating reverse proxies - now defaults to https and infers the right scheme from the IdP discovery URL), issue #48 (OIDC sign-in failed when a pre-existing Jellyfin user matched the IdP preferred_username; now links instead of failing), issue #49 (login showed 'incorrect username or password' instead of the 2FA challenge - inject.js race + relative-URL matcher), and issue #50 (email OTP UI said 6-digit but server generated 8; UI now accepts 8 across all bundled languages). New: hardened-security policy for self-service 2FA changes (SelfServiceStepUpMode tri-state, default Forced) - adding or replacing any factor now requires the user to prove a current factor, and the proof can be a TOTP / recovery code OR a passkey assertion OR an emailed step-up code, picked from the prompt modal. Other UX: pending-pairings Deny button now sticks across the next auth retry, Setup page no longer reverts the passkey list to 'Loading' after the i18n pass runs, corrupt user-data JSON now fails closed instead of silently disabling 2FA, runtime CIDR parser rejects out-of-range prefixes, OIDC re-validates cached token/userinfo endpoints per use, ntfy and Gotify now go through the SSRF-pinned client, and passkey labels are sanitized on write and escaped on render. In-place upgrade, no schema changes, no required config edits. 254/254 tests pass on .NET 9 / Jellyfin 10.11.10.

v2.5.5 - Security release. Fixes the OIDC empty-password sign-in path reported via Reddit by Throwaway-3586: newly auto-provisioned OIDC users were created without a password hash, which Jellyfin's default auth provider treats as accepting any password including empty. v2.5.5 sets a 256-bit random password on every OIDC-provisioned user at creation, so the empty-password sign-in is no longer accepted against new accounts. Also fixes the TOTP rotate endpoint (was broken in earlier versions, always rejected the current code) and bundles general security hardening across the auth pipeline (OIDC token algorithm allowlist, discovery-URL validation, recovery-code PBKDF2 bump, email-OTP storage hardening, GeoIP path validation, log scrubbing, race fixes). New optional config 'BlockEmptyPasswordLogin' (default off) extends the empty-password rejection to ALL users at the auth boundary - turn it on if your install doesn't need Jellyfin's kiosk-mode passwordless tile-click sign-in for family / guest accounts. In-place upgrade, no schema changes. One default-on behaviour change: the audit-log endpoint now requires a fresh step-up; lower StepUpLevel if that's inconvenient. 254/254 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. Smoke-tested on a live 10.11.10 host: kiosk passwordless tile-click still works, admin 2FA + passkey + Google OIDC + Security Dashboard all functional.

v2.5.4 - Bug fix release. Resolves issue #35 (Snerillinn) - Cloudflare Tunnel and reverse-proxy users were intermittently re-blocked with '[2FA] BLOCKED ... - 2FA not completed' several minutes after a successful passkey/2FA login, locking them out of the UI until a fresh re-auth. Root cause: AuthenticationEventHandler's four legitimate-bypass branches (IsDevicePreVerified, ConsumeQuickConnectPending, userDataPaired, BypassEvaluator.IsBypassed) called ChallengeStore.ApproveToken() to clear the 10-minute BlockToken TTL but did NOT call MarkTokenVerified() to set the 30-day verified flag. Subsequent SessionStarted events fire on every websocket reconnect, new browser tab, and idle-resume - and when those fire from a proxy IP that no longer matches the original bypass condition (very common behind Cloudflare Tunnel where the upstream IP can rotate), BypassEvaluator returns false on the second look, the handler walks the normal challenge path, and re-blocks the same token that was already legitimately approved minutes earlier. Fix: all four bypass branches now ALSO MarkTokenVerified(token), so the 30-day verified flag short-circuits any later SessionStarted re-evaluation regardless of which proxy IP the reconnect arrives from. Bonus: bumps Jellyfin.Controller + Jellyfin.Model SDK targets from 10.11.8 to 10.11.10, with reflection-based adaptation to the 10.11.10 IUserManager.Users (property) -> GetUsers() (method) rename - typeof(IUserManager).GetMethod('GetUsers') preferred at runtime with fallback to the legacy property via string-named GetProperty, so the same DLL still loads on 10.11.0-10.11.9 unchanged. Applied to TwoFactorAuthController.EnumerateAllUsers, StatsService.EnumerateUsers, and SecurityScoreService.EnumerateUsers. Also bumps MailKit 4.16.0 -> 4.17.0 (SMTP fixes upstream) and MaxMind.Db 5.0.0 -> 5.1.0 (GeoLite2 reader perf). 254/254 tests pass on the bumped SDK. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade - no config changes, no schema changes, no breaking changes for any reverse-proxy or direct-access topology.

v2.5.3 - Follow-up to v2.5.2 (issue #37). Completes the ABI-compatibility fix begun in v2.5.2: the audit that should have run before v2.5.2 missed one more Jellyfin manager property access in the same dashboard endpoint - _sessionManager.Sessions at TwoFactorAuthController:3679 (Overview activeSessions KPI), :2342 (RevokeSession admin endpoint), :2796 (MySessions device enrichment). Same risk class as the _userManager.Users line patched in v2.5.2 - the property's return type changed between Jellyfin 10.11.8 and 10.11.9+, so the IL-emitted callvirt threw System.MissingMethodException at runtime on a 10.11.9+ host. In practice this meant v2.5.2's dashboard fix was incomplete: a 10.11.10 server would throw on the Users line BEFORE v2.5.2 and would throw on the Sessions line AFTER v2.5.2 - the dashboard still returned 'Failed to load dashboard' from a different line. v2.5.3 actually completes the fix. New TwoFactorAuthController.EnumerateSessions() private helper mirrors the existing EnumerateAllUsers() pattern - typeof(ISessionManager).GetProperty(nameof(Sessions)).GetValue() re-binds at runtime against whatever IEnumerable shape the running Jellyfin actually exposes, items downcast to SessionInfo, with try/catch + empty-yield fallback so endpoints degrade gracefully instead of 500-ing. All three callsites routed through it. Full audit of every injected-manager surface (IUserManager, ISessionManager, IDeviceManager, IServerApplicationHost, etc.) verified zero risky direct property accesses remain after v2.5.3 - all other manager calls are method-based with stable signatures across 10.11.x. Plugin now supports Jellyfin 10.11.0 through 10.11.10+ for every code path that depends on injected manager interfaces, and is structurally resistant to future return-type refactors in 10.11.11+ because reflection bypasses static IL binding. 254/254 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade.

v2.5.2 - Bug fix release. Restores the admin Security Dashboard on Jellyfin 10.11.9+ servers. Issue #37: dashboard endpoint and the security-score 'all admins protected' factor both walked _userManager.Users via a statically-bound IL call. Between Jellyfin 10.11.8 (the ABI compiled against) and 10.11.9 the IUserManager.Users return type changed, so the plugin threw System.MissingMethodException at runtime on the newer ABI - surfaced to admins as 'Failed to load dashboard'. Fix routes both broken callsites through the same reflection-based shim already in production at TwoFactorAuthController.EnumerateAllUsers and StatsService.EnumerateUsers - Type.GetProperty(nameof(IUserManager.Users)).GetValue(_userManager) re-binds at runtime against whatever IEnumerable shape the running Jellyfin actually exposes, so it works across 10.11.8 / 10.11.9 / 10.11.10 and any future return-type change that still implements IEnumerable. Patched: TwoFactorAuthController.GetDashboardOverview enrollment-by-role loop, SecurityScoreService.AreAllAdminsProtected (security-score factor #2). Added private EnumerateUsers() helper to SecurityScoreService mirroring the existing pattern. No config / enrollment / OIDC / audit-log changes. 254/254 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade - Jellyfin 10.11.8 users see no behavioural difference, 10.11.9+ users get a working dashboard again.

v2.5.1 - OIDC enhancements + i18n bugfixes + admin UX polish. (1) Per-OIDC-provider ForceHttps toggle: when set, the redirect_uri scheme is pinned to https regardless of forwarded headers. Fixes Cloudflare Tunnel / some Caddy setups that terminate TLS upstream without propagating X-Forwarded-Proto, where the IdP would reject the http:// redirect_uri. Host trust boundary stays intact (only the scheme is overridden) so the existing redirect_uri-poisoning defence against attacker-sent X-Forwarded-Host on untrusted peers is preserved. Wired through model, controller upsert DTO, redirect-URI builder, admin form checkbox, and 8-language i18n. 4 new xUnit tests including the untrusted-host regression case. (2) OIDC Token Exchange (RFC 8693-style): new anonymous endpoint POST /TwoFactorAuth/Oidc/Exchange/{providerId} accepts an id_token from a native client (Swiftfin, Findroid, Tizen apps) that ran its own auth-code+PKCE flow against the IdP with our configured ClientId. Server re-verifies signature, issuer, audience=ClientId, expiry. Nonce check is skipped because the native client used its own nonce - the other id_token protections all still apply. Returns a one-shot bridge token the native client POSTs to /Users/AuthenticateByName, identical to the browser callback flow. Same IP-ban + 20/5min rate limit + per-user IP allowlist gates as /Oidc/Login. OidcService.VerifyIdTokenAsync's expectedNonce is now nullable; extracted FinalizeSignInAsync helper holds the shared post-id_token pipeline (userinfo merge, AMR enforcement, group allowlist, user resolution, SsoLink persistence, AuthenticationProviderId reassignment) so both CompleteAsync and ExchangeIdTokenAsync use the same code path. (3) Language picker selection-state bugfix: renderLanguagePicker rendered synchronously during each page's inline init, but _lang was still 'en' at that point because loadTranslations() is async. The <select> locked to 'English' and never resynced - even hard refresh didn't help because every page-load re-raced. Fix: after rendering, attach _readyPromise.then(syncSelectionFromResolvedLang) so the <select> value updates to _lang once translations resolve. (4) admin-script.js stays [AllowAnonymous]: an earlier internal experiment with [Authorize] broke the script load because same-origin <script src> tags carry COOKIES but NOT the Authorization: MediaBrowser header Jellyfin's auth pipeline checks. Script content is pure JavaScript UI code shipped to every admin browser anyway. (5) 15-second in-memory response cache on /Dashboard/Overview keyed by range (1w/1m/1y): endpoint runs full security-score pipeline (users + audit log + chain verify) + chart build on every hit, so tab switches and range flips would re-pay the bill. With the cache, first load computes, subsequent loads within 15s return instantly. (6) Admin Overview i18n race fix: in non-English locales the bundle fetch finished AFTER renderOverview's innerHTML write, then applyTranslations re-walked [data-i18n-key] containers and overwrote the rendered cards back to translated 'Loading...'. Three-pronged fix: gate the initial renderOverview on window.tfaI18n.ready so the bundle is loaded before the first _tr() call; defensively strip data-i18n-key from factorsGrid + enrollmentBars before setting innerHTML; wire renderLanguagePicker's onChange callback to call renderOverview() so dynamic content re-renders in the new locale. (7) update-badge.yml YAML-quoting fix so OSSF Scorecard's strict parser doesn't trip on the colon inside the commit-message literal. 254/254 tests pass (250 prior + 4 ForceHttps cases). Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade.

v2.5.0 — Major feature release: hardening, observability, i18n, indefinite trust. (1) Step-up authentication for destructive/config/everything actions with configurable level (Off/Destructive/AllConfigChanges/Everything). (2) AES-256-GCM passphrase-encrypted config exports with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600k iter) key derivation and versioned envelope. (3) Audit-chain rebuild admin action, step-up gated. (4) RequireTwoFactorToDisable hardening flag. (5) SecurityScore expanded from 5 to 12 factors (coverage, admins, enforcement, audit chain, IP ban, impossible-travel functional check, HIBP, clean-7d audit, require-to-disable, step-up, webhook, recovery codes); raw 130 pts normalized to 100 ceiling; translatable factor labels with interpolation data. (6) Admin Dashboard Overview with auth-activity time series; stacked-area chart with 1w/1m/1y range selector, hover tooltips, dashed gridlines and x-axis date labels; server-side bucket backfill so sparse 1y data still spans full range. (7) Admin Settings: server-wide DefaultLanguage picker. (8) Persistent top-strip language picker on admin page showing native language names (English/Deutsch/日本語/中文/...). (9) Typed HasPermission(IsAdministrator) admin enumeration via _userManager.Users (fixes 0/0 admin count). (10) Internationalization: 8 languages (en/de/es/fr/it/ja/pt/zh) at 664 keys each with perfect parity; tfa-i18n.js shared helper with tr()/loadTranslations()/applyTranslations()/renderLanguagePicker(); /public-config endpoint exposes default language for unauth pages; /translations/{lang} embedded-resource endpoint; all dynamic JS-rendered content deferred behind window.tfaI18n.ready promise. (11) Indefinite device trust (admin-gated AllowIndefiniteTrust config flag, default off) with per-device opt-in for trusted browsers and paired devices; 100-year trust cookie + middleware skip-expiry for IndefiniteTrust=true records. (12) admin-script.js externalized to dodge SPA loadView template-literal stripping that was breaking the dashboard with SyntaxError. (13) /Dashboard/Overview flattens DTOs to force camelCase JSON. (14) Setup page stashes /Users/Me Id into module-scope _myUserId (fixes indefinite-trust 'Something went wrong'). 250/250 tests pass. Clean build with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.13 — Bug-fix release. Promotes the v2.4.12.1 diagnostic prerelease to a stable catalog release (identical bytes, version-bumped). Fixes the 'Server not available' regression reported by FsxShader2012 and independently confirmed by Feinstone: v2.4.12's inject.js short-circuit set a sessionStorage.__tfa_pending flag on the post-login page to suppress the Jellyfin Web API barrage during the challenge-page redirect, but the challenge page (a self-contained HTML page that does NOT load inject.js) submitted /TwoFactorAuth/Verify directly without going through the inject.js shim, so the clear-on-Verify-success path never fired. When the user completed 2FA and the challenge page redirected to /web/, inject.js re-mounted on the dashboard, read the still-set flag, and short-circuited every Jellyfin Web API call with a synthetic 403 — surfacing as 'Server not available' because the apiclient interprets persistent non-2xx as the server being unreachable. The failure window depended on browser timing and Jellyfin Web build version which is why some users (including the maintainer's own setup) couldn't reproduce while others hit it every time. Fix: one-line sessionStorage.removeItem('__tfa_pending') at the top of challenge.html's inline script. By the time the user is on the challenge page the flag's job is done; clearing it here means the post-verify navigation back to /web/ is unblocked. inject.js's existing clear-on-Verify-success stays as belt-and-suspenders. Also includes the release.yml 4-part tag truncation fix carried from v2.4.12.1's prerelease — TAG derivation changed from v${VERSION%.*} (strips last .N unconditionally, mangling 4-part prereleases like 2.4.10.1 to v2.4.10) to v${VERSION%.0} (strips trailing .0 only, preserves non-zero build numbers in tags). Verified by v2.4.12.1's artifacts uploading to the correct v2.4.12.1 release instead of clobbering v2.4.12 stable. 181/181 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.12 — Bug-fix release bundling three related fixes verified end-to-end on a live Cloudflare → nginx → Jellyfin deployment (passkey + normal + OIDC + email + non-2FA logins, LAN bypass + external XFF resolution + video playback all confirmed green). (1) Closes the LAN-bypass-without-XFF hole reported in the issue #35 follow-up by FsxShader2012: SessionStarted events that fire from websocket reconnects or other non-HTTP-request contexts have no live HttpContext.Request, so v2.4.11's synchronous XFF capture saw null even though the original session came in through the configured reverse proxy. Without a guard the bypass evaluator would fall back to the peer IP (the proxy itself), match the admin's LAN-bypass CIDR, and silently ApproveToken without 2FA. New BypassEvaluator.ShouldRefuseLanBypassWhenXffMissing helper returns true only when TrustForwardedFor is on, forwardedFor is null/empty, AND the peer is inside TrustedProxyCidrs — in that state LAN bypass is refused so the session falls through to the standard 2FA / token-verified / device-paired paths. Direct LAN clients (peer NOT in TrustedProxyCidrs) keep working unchanged. 9 new regression tests cover the trigger case + present-XFF case + direct-LAN-client case + empty-trusted-proxies + empty-remoteIp + multi-CIDR + whitespace-only XFF. (2) Cuts the post-login 401 burst that was tripping SWAG's nginx-unauthorized fail2ban jail, reported in issue #36 by Wibbles42. RequestBlockerMiddleware now returns 403 instead of 401 for the blocked-token-2FA-pending case (semantically more correct since we DO know the caller — they just lack permission until 2FA completes — and crucially nginx-unauthorized's failregex matches only the literal 401 status so 403s are not counted toward brute-force bans). Response body augmented with twoFactorRequired:true so the client-side short-circuit can detect the state from any endpoint, not just the auth-path response. (3) inject.js gains a client-side short-circuit: on the first 401/403 response carrying twoFactorRequired:true, a sessionStorage flag (5-min TTL) is set and subsequent non-allowlisted fetch calls return a synthetic 403 immediately without touching the network. Allowlist mirrors RequestBlockerMiddleware.AlwaysAllowedPaths verbatim so the user can still reach /TwoFactorAuth/Login, /Verify, /Authenticate. Flag clears on successful Verify/Authenticate response. XHR shim only recognises the marker (no short-circuit — synthesising XHR completion events is too brittle for native jellyfin-apiclient consumers); the server-side 401→403 covers any XHR call that races ahead. Combined effect: per-login 401s drop from ~15 to 0, and the residual blocked-token responses are 403s that fail2ban's status-401-only regex never counts. Admins on SWAG / any nginx-unauthorized setup can keep the default maxretry=5 with no constraint on user count behind a shared source IP (Cloudflare, CGNAT, family network). 181/181 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.11 — Bug-fix release. (1) Fixes the LAN-bypass-via-reverse-proxy hole reported in the issue #35 follow-up (FsxShader2012). AuthenticationEventHandler.OnSessionStarted called BypassEvaluator.Evaluate with forwardedFor=null, so the bypass evaluator could not walk X-Forwarded-For right-to-left at authentication time. With LAN bypass enabled, every reverse-proxy request whose TCP peer IP (the proxy's address) fell inside a configured LAN-bypass CIDR was treated as a LAN client regardless of the real upstream client IP — silently skipping 2FA for any external user behind a trusted reverse proxy. Fix: inject IHttpContextAccessor into AuthenticationEventHandler and snapshot X-Forwarded-For synchronously inside OnSessionStarted (before the Task.Run handoff, since the background task outlives the HTTP request and reading HttpContext after handoff would race with request completion); plumb the captured header through HandleSessionAsync into BypassEvaluator.Evaluate, which already implemented the SEC-H2 right-to-left walk in PickRealClientIp. The middleware path (TwoFactorEnforcementMiddleware) already read XFF correctly via the same IHttpContextAccessor; only the session-event path was missing it. (2) Promotes v2.4.10.1's diagnostic-build changes into the catalog: TwoFactorEnforcementMiddleware now sets Accept-Encoding: identity on auth-path requests to suppress downstream response compression that would otherwise garble the buffered auth response, and the LooksLikeAuthResponse failure log now surfaces first-8-bytes hex, first-100-chars preview, Content-Encoding header, and Content-Type header so future response-shape mismatches are identifiable in a single round-trip. v2.4.10.1 confirmed working for FsxShader2012's original stuck-on-login symptom (gzip was the culprit); this release bundles those same changes for everyone. 172/172 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.10 — Bug-fix release. Fixes issue #35 (FsxShader2012 reported stuck-on-login spinner with 2FA-enabled users). Root cause: TwoFactorEnforcementMiddleware's LooksLikeAuthResponse sniff was case-sensitive (Ordinal) and checked only the PascalCase markers "AccessToken"/"User"/"SessionInfo". Some users' Jellyfin setups (response-wrapping middleware in their stack, or custom JSON naming policy) emit camelCase keys ("accessToken" etc.), which silently failed the substring check. The middleware then passed the auth response straight through with the token intact, RequestBlockerMiddleware blocked subsequent calls token-scoped, and the 2FA challenge UI never rendered. Fix: switched the three substring comparisons from StringComparison.Ordinal to StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase, aligning the sniff with the downstream JsonSerializer.Deserialize which already uses PropertyNameCaseInsensitive=true. The three-key requirement (SEC v2.4 L6) is preserved — third-party admin endpoints returning JSON that mentions just AccessToken+User still won't get pulled into the 2FA flow. The v2.4.9 diagnostic Info log is retained so any future stranger response shape (snake_case, wrapped JSON, etc.) surfaces immediately. Note: v2.4.9 was a diagnostic-only pre-release (not in this catalog) used to gather the data that led to this fix. 172/172 tests pass (6 new LooksLikeAuthResponseTests pinning PascalCase, camelCase, mixed-case, missing-key, oversized, and HTML cases). In-place upgrade.

v2.4.8 — Bug-fix release. Two real defects reported in issue #29 (Authelia + Gmail SMTP setup). (1) SMTP test email over port 465 silently failed because System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient.EnableSsl=true triggers STARTTLS rather than Implicit TLS — port 465 expects a TLS handshake BEFORE any SMTP commands. Fix: migrated to MailKit. New PickSocketOptions helper maps port 465 → SslOnConnect, port 587 → StartTls, other ports + UseSsl=true → StartTlsWhenAvailable. (2) OIDC sign-in via Authelia rejected users as 'not part of allowed groups' even when scopes included groups. Root cause: the plugin only read claims from the id_token JWT, but Authelia (default config), Keycloak (most realms), and Authentik emit groups/email/email_verified only at the /userinfo endpoint. Fix: after id_token verification, the plugin now fetches /userinfo with the access_token and merges any groups, roles, email, email_verified, and username claims before the AllowedGroups check and ResolveUserAsync. Validated end-to-end on a real Authelia 4.39 instance (same IdP family as the reporter) plus a real Gmail smtp.gmail.com:465 send. Ships MailKit + MimeKit + BouncyCastle.Cryptography in the fat package (~7.2MB total). 166/166 tests pass (5 new SMTP socket-option tests, 6 new userinfo extraction tests). In-place upgrade.

v2.4.7 — Bug-fix release. Fixes the OIDC redirect_uri http:// bug reported in issue #28 (Kanidm + cloudflared). Root cause: BuildRedirectUri's proxy-header check required BOTH X-Forwarded-Proto AND X-Forwarded-Host to be present before honoring either. Reverse-proxy setups that only emit X-Forwarded-Proto (cloudflared, many nginx configs, some Caddy setups) fell through to Request.Scheme which is 'http' when TLS terminates upstream; the IdP correctly rejected per the OAuth spec exact-match comparison. Fix: each forwarded header is now evaluated independently — X-Forwarded-Proto honored regardless of X-Forwarded-Host's presence, and vice versa. The proxyTrusted gate (peer must be in TrustedProxyCidrs) is unchanged for BOTH header checks, so attackers connecting directly still cannot inject either header. The URL-construction logic was extracted to a pure static helper OidcRedirectUriBuilder so it's testable without HttpContext mocking, and 5 regression tests were added covering happy path, the issue #28 fix, and two security-boundary regressions (untrusted-peer Proto + Host spoofing must remain ignored). 155/155 tests pass. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.6 — Bug-fix release. Fixes the 'logged out every couple of minutes' loop reported in issue #27. Root cause: AuthenticationEventHandler subscribes to ISessionManager.SessionStarted, which fires not only on initial login but also on websocket reconnects, new tabs, idle-resume, and reverse-proxy WS drops (Traefik, Caddy, nginx). Once the 2-minute pre-verify window expired, the handler's failsafe BlockToken re-blocked the user's active access token; RequestBlockerMiddleware then 401'd every subsequent request, the client retried, a new SessionStarted fired, repeat. Fix: ChallengeStore now tracks tokens that have completed 2FA at least once in this process lifetime (30-day TTL, capped + swept). AuthenticationEventHandler skips the failsafe block and the session-end for verified tokens, treating those SessionStarted events as reconnects (audit log Method='reconnect'). The failsafe still fires for genuinely unverified tokens. Secondary fix: Jellyfin 10.11.9 changed IUserManager.Users's return type in a non-ABI-compatible way; StatsService.ComputeAsync and the AdminForceLogout 'last admin' guard now use reflection-based enumeration so they no longer throw MissingMethodException on 10.11.9 hosts. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.5 — Dependency-refresh + README polish. No plugin behavior changes (DLL functionally identical to v2.4.4). GitHub Actions deps refreshed via Dependabot: actions/checkout 5 to 6, actions/setup-dotnet 4.3 to 5.2, actions/attest-build-provenance 2.4 to 4.1, sigstore/cosign-installer 3.9 to 4.1 (with cosign binary pinned to v2.4.0 to preserve --output-signature/--output-certificate flags that Scorecard's Signed-Releases check needs), github/codeql-action 3.x to 4.35.5 (coordinated bump across init/analyze/upload-sarif after Dependabot's grouped PR shipped an inconsistent diff). Test deps: Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.12 to 18.5.1. Held back deliberately: Jellyfin.Controller/Model 10.11.8 to 10.11.9 (10.11.9 changed IUserManager.Users in a breaking way; pinned to 10.11.8 until planned SDK upgrade). README: test-count badge 125 to 150, expanded repo topics to include passkey/webauthn/oidc/sso/fido2. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.4 — OpenSSF Scorecard hygiene release. No behavior changes (plugin DLL byte-identical to v2.4.3). LICENSE rewritten to canonical MIT so GitHub's classifier recognizes it (the previous file had appended Third-party + Summary sections that broke detection); commentary moved to a new THIRD-PARTY.md. .clusterfuzzlite/Dockerfile no longer references the non-existent gcr.io/oss-fuzz-base/base-builder-csharp image (the upstream CFLite csharp docs cite an image that was never published) — swapped to the real base-builder pinned by SHA256. release.yml now uploads the SLSA provenance attestation as a *.intoto.jsonl release asset so Scorecard's Signed-Releases check sees provenance directly (previously it only lived in GitHub's attestation registry). In-place upgrade.

v2.4.3 — Supply-chain + fuzz-testing release. No behavior changes (passkey, TOTP, OIDC, lockout, sessions, audit log all unchanged). SLSA build provenance: release zips now ship a signed in-toto attestation linking each artifact to its commit SHA + GitHub Actions workflow run. Verifiable via `gh attestation verify --owner ZL154 <zip>`. Brings the OpenSSF Scorecard Signed-Releases check to full credit. Fuzz testing: new tests/Jellyfin.Plugin.TwoFactorAuth.Fuzz/ project + SharpFuzz + ClusterFuzzLite scaffolding drives libFuzzer against BypassEvaluator.PickRealClientIp (the X-Forwarded-For parser that handles attacker-controlled HTTP headers). cflite_pr.yml runs a 5-minute fuzz on every PR touching src/ or the fuzz harness; crashes surface as SARIF in the Security tab. Internal: csproj pinned Jellyfin.Controller/Model to exact 10.11.8 (was 10.11.* wildcard) so a new 10.11.x patch can't silently break the release build. In-place upgrade.

v2.4.2 — Code quality release. No behavior changes (passkey, TOTP, OIDC, lockout, sessions, audit log all unchanged). Cleared every analyzer warning the build was emitting: silenced 7 pure perf-only Roslyn rules (CA1848/1822/1805/1845/1865/1859/1869) in .editorconfig with documented justifications, fixed 13 correctness/clarity warnings in source (CA1001 IDisposable on OidcLoginTokenStore + OidcService so cleanup timers release cleanly, CA1305 culture-invariant ToString on Retry-After + OTP code, CA2249 IndexOf -> Contains, CA1835 Memory<byte> ReadAsync overload, CA2012 await ValueTask in admin RevokeSession, CA1806 explicit discard, CA1725 interface param names, CA1711 documented SuppressMessage, CA5350 SHA-1 annotated per-symbol with HIBP k-anonymity rationale). Enabled <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors> so future regressions can't ship silently. Added coverage baseline via coverlet.collector (current: 7.8% lines / 6.6% branches). In-place upgrade.

v2.4.1 — Bugfix + Fido2NetLib 4.0 migration. Bugfix: clicking Begin Setup then navigating away no longer leaves an account half-enrolled and locked out when EnforcementScope=All; TotpEnabled is now flipped only on ConfirmTotp success, and the auth-time gate (middleware + provider) checks (TotpEnabled && TotpVerified) instead of TotpEnabled alone, so any v2.4.0 rows already stuck in that state are auto-rescued on next sign-in. TwoFactorAuthProvider also now honours EnforcementScope (Optional/Admins-only/All) instead of the legacy RequireForAllUsers flag. Library: Fido2NetLib 3.0.1 to 4.0.1 — params-object API, exception-based failure, WebAuthn Level 3 fields (backup-eligibility, attestation format, transports) exposed for future policy work. Ships three new transitive deps (NSec.Cryptography, System.Formats.Cbor, Microsoft.Bcl.Memory) in the fat package. UI: EnforcementScope dropdown is now styled like the rest of the settings page. In-place upgrade; no migration.

v2.4.0 — Security hardening, per-role policy, breach-password check, and 'Where am I signed in?'. Security: 10 fixes from internal review (email enumeration on 2FA endpoints rate-limited, atomic challenge consumption to close a passkey replay window, auth-path check hoisted before body buffering, audit-log label sanitization, passkey assertion rate limit, plus L-tier hardening). Policy: new EnforcementScope setting (Optional / Admins only / All users) replaces the old all-or-nothing toggle — Admins-only is the recommended pattern for shared media servers. HIBP (opt-in): on sign-in, the first 5 hex chars of SHA-1(password) are sent to api.pwnedpasswords.com (k-anonymity); a breach hit writes an audit entry and warning log but never blocks sign-in; fails open on outage. Sessions: Setup page now shows a 'Where am I signed in?' panel of your active devices and lets you self-revoke any of them. In-place upgrade.

v2.3.2 — Dependency refresh + supply chain hardening. Ships the dependabot updates that landed after v2.3.1 was cut: QuestPDF 2024.12 to 2026.5 (recovery code PDF rendering), Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens + System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt 8.0 to 8.18 (OIDC JWT validation), MaxMind.Db 4.1 to 5.0 (GeoIP for impossible-travel detection). Repo: NuGet packages.lock.json now committed for both csproj files; CI restores in locked-mode so transitive dep drift fails fast. Workflow Token-Permissions tightened to read-all top-level with per-job scoped writes only where actually needed. No plugin code changes since v2.3.1 — this release is purely the merged dep updates and supply chain work. In-place upgrade.

v2.3.1 — Security hardening + supply chain. Real fixes: SSRF allowlist for webhook delivery is now correctly visible to the HttpClient ConnectCallback across awaits (was silently broken due to ThreadStatic vs AsyncLocal); OIDC token-exchange request body is now disposed deterministically; full email addresses are no longer written to plaintext logs (masked to a***@example.com). Supply chain: every GitHub Action SHA-pinned, Docker SDK image pinned by digest, release zip is now Sigstore-signed (verify with cosign verify-blob), CodeQL + OpenSSF Scorecard scanning every push, branch protection on main, dependabot active. Underlying NuGet deps refreshed via merged dependabot PRs. No breaking changes; in-place upgrade.

v2.3.0 — Security maintenance and forced enrollment. Fixed some security issues, strengthened sign-in handling, added a proper forced-enrollment flow when Require 2FA for all users is enabled, improved OIDC/SSO reliability, and fixed a Settings-page layout overlap. Public notes are intentionally high-level.

v2.2.3 — PDF font fix. Recovery-code PDF now actually renders the text. v2.2.2 swapped the font from Fonts.SegoeUI to 'Lato' thinking QuestPDF auto-loaded Lato — it doesn't, the constant is just a name. Skia's fallback found nothing usable inside the Jellyfin Docker container (no system fonts) and rendered every glyph as an empty box. Lato-Regular and Lato-Bold are now embedded as resources in the plugin DLL and registered with QuestPDF's FontManager in the RecoveryCodePdfService static constructor. Works on any container regardless of installed system fonts. No breaking changes; in-place upgrade.

v2.2.2 — UX polish. Recovery-code PDF now renders correctly inside Linux containers (was producing empty glyph boxes due to Windows-only fonts; switched to QuestPDF's bundled Lato font). 2FA challenge page now exposes a Recovery code tab alongside Authenticator and Email so a user without their authenticator can sign in directly. All Setup-page confirmation prompts (regenerate codes, revoke device / app password / trusted browser, disable 2FA, emergency lockout) now use a dark-themed in-page modal instead of the browser native confirm() popup. No breaking changes; in-place upgrade.

v2.2.1 — Multi-architecture support. Recovery-code PDF generation now works on linux-x64, linux-arm64, and linux-musl-x64 containers (previously only linux-x64 native libs shipped). Runtime architecture + libc detection in RecoveryCodePdfService picks the right RID's native libs at startup, copies them next to the plugin DLL where QuestPDF probes, and loads them in dependency order. PDF init wraps in try/catch so a failed native load no longer takes the rest of the plugin down. Build pipeline rewritten as a fat-package builder + new GitHub Actions workflow that builds inside dotnet sdk:9.0 Docker. Multi-arch fix contributed by @glauciocampos.

v2.2 — Hardening + performance. Internal hardening pass on the auth pipeline (cookie attributes behind reverse proxies, stricter handling of forwarded headers, additional input bounds). Performance: in-memory caches for hot paths (per-user data, audit log, parsed CIDRs, patched /web/ index), background-flushed audit log instead of per-event rewrite, faster login latency by replacing a polling wait with immediate signaling. Operational: trusted-browser cookie now carries the Secure flag correctly when Jellyfin is behind a TLS-terminating proxy (Cloudflare, Caddy, nginx) — set TrustForwardedFor + TrustedProxyCidrs in plugin settings to enable. Audit log is now compact JSON on disk; existing logs continue to read fine. No breaking changes; in-place upgrade.

v2.1 — Passkey primary login. NEW: 'Sign in with passkey' button on the standard login page — users with a passkey registered can sign in with one click (type username → click button → authenticator prompt → done), no password needed. Uses the same one-shot bridge-token mechanism as OIDC. WebAuthn requires a secure context (HTTPS or localhost); button is hidden otherwise. FIX: inject.js now sent with Cache-Control: no-store so CDN/reverse-proxy caching doesn't pin old script after plugin upgrades — if you were on a 24h Cloudflare cache, new buttons + fixes now appear immediately. Heads-up: Cloudflare's default Page Rules may still cache JS; add a Bypass rule for /TwoFactorAuth/* to guarantee immediate propagation.

v2.0.0 — Jellyfin Security. Plugin rename from 'Two-Factor Authentication' to 'Jellyfin Security' (GUID unchanged, upgrades in place). NEW: OIDC / SSO sign-in (Google, Microsoft/Entra, Apple, Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak, PocketID, Cloudflare Access, or any OIDC-compliant IdP) with PKCE S256, id_token signature + issuer + audience + nonce validation, optional AMR-based IdP-MFA enforcement, optional group allowlist, per-provider auto-create toggle. NEW: brute-force IP banning — configurable threshold + window + duration, persisted across restarts, LAN / trusted-proxy / exempt CIDRs never banned, admin IP Bans tab lists/unbans. NEW: impossible-travel detection — Haversine distance vs time exceeding configured km/h fires a notification via existing channels, uses GeoLite2-City. NEW: per-user IP allowlist — pin high-value accounts to specific CIDRs, self-service in Setup. NEW: login-page provider buttons, Linked Sign-In Methods card in user Setup, pill-style admin tab bar, new Sign-in Methods and IP Bans tabs, new Settings sections for brute-force + impossible-travel. SECURITY: X-Forwarded-Host/Proto only honoured when direct peer is in TrustedProxyCidrs; rate limit on /Oidc/Login (20/5min); bridge HTML uses JsonSerializer.Serialize for JS-context injection + strict CSP + Cache-Control no-store; returnUrl validated to same-origin relative paths. BUG FIXES: TOTP replay cache cleared on new-secret generation (fixed 'Invalid code' false-positive when setup ran twice); Setup page no longer shows NOT SET UP for non-admin users; default-auth provider delegation now uses IRequiresResolvedUser correctly (Jellyfin 10.11's DefaultAuthenticationProvider throws NotImplementedException on the plain Authenticate overload); provider no longer throws AuthenticationException carrying 2FA challenge JSON (Jellyfin ate the payload — middleware path handles the challenge response body now). Bundles IdentityModel.OidcClient, Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens, System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt in addition to the existing v1.4 deps.

CRITICAL fix for 1.4.0/1.4.1: the /web/ index page was rendered as raw gzip bytes in the browser (wall of garbage, Jellyfin UI refused to load) when Kestrel served the pre-compressed index.html.gz static asset. IndexHtmlInjectionMiddleware now strips Accept-Encoding on the incoming /web/ request so the upstream responds with identity-encoded HTML we can safely inject into. Only applied to /web/ /web /web/index.html — other assets still compress normally. Upgrade if you saw mojibake on the web UI.

Bug-fix release. CRITICAL: Samsung Tizen / Smart TV clients behind a reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx, Cloudflare, etc) couldn't sign in after the v1.4 upgrade — their AuthenticateByName requests arrive at the server without X-Emby-Device-Id or a parseable X-Emby-Authorization, so the plugin couldn't extract a deviceId and the paired-device/registered-device bypasses never fired, forcing the TV through a 2FA challenge it can't render. Fixed: the enforcement middleware now falls back to reading SessionInfo.DeviceId from Jellyfin's own auth response body when request headers don't carry a deviceId. RegisteredDeviceIds lookup now uses the same normalisation as PairedDevices so Jellyfin Web UA-hash deviceIds match across session-timestamp suffix changes (Tizen webview restarts). Also removed leftover dev-only diagnostic log lines accumulated during this investigation.

v1.4 — Passkeys + safety net. PASSKEYS / WebAuthn as additive 2nd factor (Face ID / Touch ID / Windows Hello / YubiKey) — register from Setup, sign in with one tap from any browser; native apps still use device pairing (WebAuthn is browser-only). USER SELF-SERVICE: emergency lockout button (terminate every session, revoke every device, force recovery code on next sign-in), TOTP secret rotation without admin (current code + recovery code), recovery codes PDF + print, autocomplete=one-time-code on OTP input, QR-pair-from-phone (reverse of TV pairing). ADMIN TOOLS: new Overview tab with adoption stats, new Diagnostics tab with green/red checklist, new Rate Limits tab with bucket-trip log, force-logout per user (with last-admin guard), bulk actions (reset 2FA, rotate recovery, revoke paired/trusted, force logout), search/filter Users tab, expandable per-user details row, per-user GDPR JSON export, audit-log CSV export, dashboard-sidebar entry, expand/collapse for long Trusted/Paired/Sessions lists. WEBHOOK + ALERTS: POST every notable event to a configurable URL with HMAC-SHA256 signature (timestamp.body) and X-2FA-Timestamp header; auto-reshapes for Discord and Slack URLs; SSRF guard rejects RFC1918/loopback/link-local/cloud-metadata. Suspicious-login alerts on first-seen ASN/country (admin drops MaxMind GeoLite2 .mmdb files into config). SECURITY: audit log hash chain (tamper detection), per-user concurrent session cap, NAT-hairpin self-IP bypass (opt-in), configurable pre-verify window + trust cookie TTL. v1.4 audit performed in-flight: 4 High + 8 Medium + 1 Low fixed (Passkeys/Diagnose admin-only, ForceRecoveryOnNextLogin enforced, QrPair deviceId cross-check, ClientLog rate-limited+capped, webhook SSRF guard, last-admin force-logout guard, PDF resource cap + filename sanitize, SelfIp rejects private addresses, bulk audit chain entries, TOTP-rotate notification, webhook timestamp+HMAC contract, dashboard-nav admin-gate, webhook-test rate-limit). Bundles Fido2NetLib, MaxMind.Db, QuestPDF + Linux x64 native libs (libsodium, libQuestPdfSkia). Windows / macOS need Docker or manual native install — see README.

Security hardening release. Trust cookie now signs deviceId+expiry into the payload (prevents device-substitution bypass) and rotates on every use. Token-approval race bound to (userId, deviceId, token) and single-consume. Recovery codes upgraded to PBKDF2-SHA256 with per-code salt (legacy SHA-256 codes still validate). Open redirect in /Challenge?return= closed (same-origin enforcement). DeviceId comparisons now case-sensitive (Ordinal). Pairing approve refuses Guid.Empty/empty-deviceId. RegisteredDeviceIds capped at 50 with 128-char printable-ASCII validation. IsAuthPath anchored to ^/Users/ instead of substring match. Anti-clickjacking headers on all embedded pages (X-Frame-Options DENY + CSP frame-ancestors). Rate limiter now reverse-proxy aware via X-Forwarded-For + TrustedProxyCidrs, IPv6 bucketed by /64. Per-user rate limit on /Verify (15/15min) in addition to per-IP. /Pairings/Initiate input sanitized (length-cap, control-char strip). inject.js redirects to hardcoded path instead of trusting body ChallengePageUrl. TestSmtp no longer leaks ex.Message. Device revocation now wipes pre-verify state and logs out access tokens. PairConfirm has replay protection. API keys stored as SHA-256 hash (auto-migration from legacy plaintext). CookieSigner.Verify length-checks before FixedTimeEquals. Settings tile renders correctly in themed drawers. Diagnostic log chatter moved to Debug.

CRITICAL FIX: failing 2FA on one device no longer signs you out on all other devices. Pre-verification and blocking are now scoped to (user, device) instead of user-wide. CRITICAL FIX: Swiftfin/Findroid 2FA bypass when another browser had just completed 2FA — caused by a user-scoped 2-minute pre-verification window that piggy-backed onto any device connecting. App passwords now ACTUALLY work for native clients — implemented as a fast-path in IAuthenticationProvider instead of response rewriting. Submit your app password in the native app's password field; server accepts it and skips the default provider. QR pairing: each pending device can be approved by scanning a QR on a phone that's already signed in. New settings tile on preferences page, back button on challenge page. Security: rate-limited and lockout-checked app password attempts, atomic pending-pairing approval, device-scoped state, ConfigChanged audit category, dead code removed, paired-device revoke now ends live sessions immediately, full challenge state wiped on 2FA disable.

Native client support: app passwords (PBKDF2-SHA256 hashed, revocable) for Swiftfin/Findroid users with a Jellyfin password. Device pairing for passwordless users: failed native-client logins register as pending requests, user approves from Setup page. Quick Connect pass-through for TVs. Redesigned Setup page: status dashboard, TOTP enrollment, recovery codes, email backup, pending device approvals, paired devices, app passwords, trusted browsers, active sessions. Sidebar entry uses AchievementBadges navMenuOption pattern for consistent theming. Settings page tile. Admin Users tab fixed (was 404'ing on System/Configuration). Security audit fixes: atomic read-modify-write for concurrent user data updates, rate-limited app-password verification, bounded pending-pairing dict (5000 global, 50/user), chunked-encoding request body support, fail-closed (503) on middleware exceptions, pending pairings cleared on 2FA disable.

Fix: failed-login latency. RequestBlockerMiddleware was running Jellyfin's claim resolver on every request whose X-Emby-Authorization header was set, including unauthenticated AuthenticateByName POSTs (which carry the header for client metadata, not auth). Now we only run the claim resolver when an actual Token=... segment or X-Emby-Token header is present. Wrong passwords now fail fast. Fix: 'Two-Factor Auth' link now appears in BOTH the main side drawer and the Settings page tile list. Selectors broadened so it survives custom themes (STARTRACK, etc.).

Fix: passwordless / quick-profile login now triggers 2FA. The injected script now intercepts BOTH fetch and XHR auth responses; when the server returns 401 with twoFactorRequired:true, the browser is redirected to the challenge page automatically. Works for the manual login form, the avatar quick-login flow, and any other auth path. Fix: signed-in users now get a 'Two-Factor Auth' link in Jellyfin's user menu so they can find the Setup page without knowing the URL. Fix: failed-login spinner — clarified the failure path so wrong-credential 401s pass through to Jellyfin's normal error UI instead of stalling.

CRITICAL FIX for v1.2.0: PluginConfiguration.UserEmailAddresses was a Dictionary which Jellyfin's XML serializer cannot handle. Adding the new TotpIssuerName field triggered a config rewrite on every request, crashing the entire HTTP pipeline (white-screen Jellyfin web UI). Replaced with an XML-serializable List<UserEmailEntry> plus GetUserEmail/SetUserEmail helpers. Existing per-user email entries WILL be lost on upgrade — admins need to re-enter them in the Users tab.

Major release. Recovery codes (10 single-use backups). Email OTP via SMTP. Per-IP rate limiting on Verify and Authenticate endpoints. Per-challenge attempt limit. Generic error messages prevent account enumeration. Atomic file writes. Recovery codes marked used immediately on validation. Cookie SameSite=Strict + persistent HMAC key. Admin trusted-devices view with revoke. Per-user email management. Lockout countdown UI. Login flow fixed for non-2FA users. Push notifications wired to ntfy/Gotify. Comprehensive admin UI overhaul. Full README rewrite.

Per-device 30-day trust via signed HTTP-only cookie. After 2FA verification on a browser, that browser gets a __2fa_trust cookie (HMAC-signed, HttpOnly, Secure, Lax). Subsequent logins from that browser skip 2FA for 30 days; new browsers/devices still need 2FA. Cookie ties to a server-side trust record so revoking the device in admin invalidates the cookie.

Fix blank page after 2FA login. Pre-verified flag now lasts 2 minutes (non-consuming) so all sessions from a login attempt are allowed — WebSocket connects + HTTP sessions were previously re-blocking the user immediately. 30-day trust now checks 'any recent verification' instead of strict device ID match, since Jellyfin generates different device IDs for different session types.

Remember device for 30 days. After completing /TwoFactorAuth/Login, the device is auto-trusted — subsequent logins from the same browser skip 2FA until the 30-day window expires. No more re-typing the code on every refresh. Trusted devices visible and revocable in the Setup page.

Actually block non-2FA logins. RequestBlockerMiddleware now calls context.AuthenticateAsync('CustomAuthentication') explicitly to resolve the user claims, since our middleware runs before Jellyfin's auth handler in the pipeline. Previously context.User was always empty and the block never fired.

Actually enforce 2FA. New RequestBlockerMiddleware returns 401 for every authenticated API call from users who logged in without completing 2FA — so normal login no longer lets them through, they must use /TwoFactorAuth/Login. Button on login page now matches Jellyfin's native style (neutral, not bright blue) and properly captures the username at click-time. Login card sized better on wide screens.

Reliable login integration. Instead of fragile HTTP interception, the injected script now adds a visible 'Sign in with Two-Factor Authentication' button directly under Jellyfin's normal Sign In button. Username is auto-filled from the form as you type. Works regardless of how Jellyfin's web client internally handles login requests.

Improved integrated login interception. Injected script now patches BOTH fetch and XMLHttpRequest (Jellyfin ApiClient uses XHR), logs to browser console, and adds a MutationObserver form listener as fallback. Server-side logs confirm when injection happens.

Auto-redirect from Jellyfin's default login. Inject script now intercepts the standard login form — if the typed username has 2FA enabled, it redirects to /TwoFactorAuth/Login with username pre-filled. Users no longer need to know the separate login URL.

Fix TOTP secrets invalidating on restart. Switched from Jellyfin's ephemeral IDataProtectionProvider to AES-GCM encryption with a persistent 32-byte key stored at /config/plugins/configurations/TwoFactorAuth/secret.key. TOTP enrollments now survive Jellyfin restarts. NOTE: Existing enrollments must be re-done once after upgrading.

Diagnostic build for /Authenticate endpoint. Wraps entire endpoint in try/catch, logs every step, returns actual error message in 500 responses so login page can display it. Most likely diagnosis: data protection key lost between plugin restarts (stored ephemeral) — users may need to re-enroll TOTP.

Complete 2FA login flow. New /TwoFactorAuth/Login page has username + password + TOTP code fields. Authenticating through it pre-marks the user so the enforcement event handler lets the session persist. POST /TwoFactorAuth/Authenticate endpoint validates TOTP and calls ISessionManager.AuthenticateNewSession atomically.

Event-based enforcement. Subscribes to ISessionManager.SessionStarted which fires server-side on every successful login. When 2FA-enabled user logs in without bypass, their session is immediately ended server-side. Works regardless of middleware/routing. UX: login appears to succeed then immediately fails — user must verify via /TwoFactorAuth/Verify to get valid session.

Content-shape detection: middleware now inspects any POST response that contains AccessToken+User+SessionInfo (the standard Jellyfin auth response shape) regardless of path. This catches /Users/AuthenticateByName, /Users/AuthenticateWithQuickConnect, and any custom auth endpoint.
Log every POST request unconditionally so we can find the exact auth endpoint path.

More diagnostic logging. Startup filter now logs when invoked. Middleware logs every POST containing 'user'/'auth'/'login' in path so we can find the actual auth endpoint. Path matching loosened to EndsWith so it handles /api prefix.
Added detailed diagnostic logging to enforcement middleware so login flow can be debugged via Jellyfin logs.
Fix 401 on /TwoFactorAuth/Setup — HTML page is now served anonymously (JavaScript inside uses stored Jellyfin token for API calls).

Full end-to-end web login flow. Browser is automatically redirected to the 2FA challenge page when a challenge is required. After verification, credentials are stored and user is returned to Jellyfin web UI. Middleware now stashes the auth response during challenge instead of revoking, so verification returns a real working session.

Added 2FA login enforcement via middleware and user-facing setup page. When enabled, logins for users with TOTP enabled now return a challenge instead of a session token. Setup page at /TwoFactorAuth/Setup lets users enroll themselves.

Removed API Keys tab (Jellyfin's built-in API keys already bypass user auth). Fixed tab switching (CSS wasn't applied because styles were in <head> which Jellyfin strips). Scoped all styles to #TwoFactorAuth to not leak into other pages.
Fix config page not loading (div ID now matches page name), proper assembly versioning so installed plugin shows correct version.
Fix admin config page format.
Fix startup crash.
Initial release.
